description.narrative: The project aims to address critical challenges in Pakistan's power sector, which are exacerbated by a complex macroeconomic environment, the growing circular debt, and inefficiencies in the transmission sector. High system losses, weak revenue collection, outdated infrastructure, and governance gaps have placed a strain on both fiscal stability and the reliability of electricity supply. To help address these challenges, the project will advance the Government of Pakistan's agenda to strengthen grid stability, improve energy security, and build climate resilience. It will increase transmission capacity to deliver clean, reliable, and cost-effective electricity that supports sustainable economic growth, while enhancing the overall management of the national transmission system. This will be achieved by (i) expanding the high-voltage transmission network in Punjab to complete 500-kilovolt (kV) and 220 kV transmission line (T/L) loops, thereby ensuring adequate transmission capacity to transfer renewable energy to the major load centers in the densely populated Islamabad and Faisalabad areas; and (ii) supporting priority reforms of state-owned enterprises (SOEs) by improving the institutional, financial, system planning, and project management capacity of the National Grid Company of Pakistan Limited (NGC)formerly National Transmission & Despatch Company Limited (NTDC) along with strengthening its public outreach and communications. In addition, the project will integrate gender equality and climate resilience measures, ensuring these cross-cutting priorities are embedded in its design and implementation. In this way, the project will contribute to Pakistan's broader goal of building a sustainable, efficient, and inclusive energy sector.
